cases.why: Labour-disputes 19 ¶¶1–3 requires prior conciliation but makes it optional for a defendant abroad or employer bankruptcy/judicial settlement, and excludes the specified statutory public-service disputes. Ask whether any of those conditions applies and whether this is a consequential additional request covered by CPCA 510 ¶1. Those facts are unknown, so absence of the record required by labour-disputes 37 ¶1 does not yet justify an unconditional stepMissing conclusion.

cases.why: CPCA 504 ¶1 and 405 ¶1 give an unextended full-period endpoint of 11 June, before this petition. Ask whether non-working days extended that endpoint under 405 ¶¶3–4, and whether force majeure or disruption of justice supports relief under 322 ¶¶1–2. Without an applicable extension or relief, 504 ¶1 imposes forfeiture of the right to sue, an inadmissibility ground under 67 ¶1.

cases.why: CPCA 504 ¶1 and 405 ¶1 bring the unextended full-period endpoint to 13 June. Ask whether that day was wholly or partly non-working and when the first following working day occurred under 405 ¶¶3–4; the supplied texts do not establish the weekly rest calendar. If the petition was beyond the extended endpoint, also ask about the circumstances permitting relief under 322 ¶¶1–2 before applying forfeiture.
